findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how reader-process catch-up reconciles AC4 (next-create findability, no background process) with the 'no indexing/model work on the write path' constraint — name whether catch-up embedding runs synchronously inside the next `create`, and bound its cost (the AC2 500ms bound is scoped to a warm index) — leaving the concrete choice to the ADR.
evidence: AC4: 'A newly created ticket is findable by the next create on the same clone without any background process running.'
Constraint: 'No indexing work is spawned from the write path; catch-up happens in the reader's process on next use, keyed by the tickets-branch HEAD SHA, with full rebuild on any mismatch.'
Constraint: 'Model calls are bounded and off the write path: summarization and embedding run in a batch step.'
AC2 bounds p95 500ms only 'when the index is warm', so a create that triggers catch-up embedding of the new ticket is explicitly outside the timing bound and its cost is unstated.
findings.finding: The catch-up mechanism as specified leaves an unreconciled tension: AC4 requires a just-created ticket to be findable by the NEXT `create` via reader-process catch-up with no background process, which forces a summarize+embed call to run during that next `create` invocation — but the Constraints state 'No indexing work is spawned from the write path' and 'summarization and embedding run in a batch step' off the write path. Since the next `create` is itself a write-path invocation, the epic does not say how catch-up embedding coexists with the no-model-calls-on-write-path constraint, nor is this cold-catch-up create bounded (AC2's p95 500ms is scoped to 'when the index is warm').
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria (AC4) vs. 'Constraints every design must satisfy' (catch-up / Model-calls bullets)
scenarios: Clone A creates ticket T1, then immediately runs `create` for T2; catch-up must embed T1 synchronously inside the T2 create for AC4 to hold, running a model call on the write path.
A batch of N creates with no reader in between means the next create pays catch-up embedding for all N changed tickets, with no stated bound.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State, per affected arm (compose-time suggestion, index catch-up/rebuild, on-demand judge), the disposition the caller surfaces on failure using an explicit disposition word (e.g. advisory field degrades to empty = non-fatal; judge LLM throttle stays retryable/WAIT_AND_RETRY and is not swallowed by the non-blocking path).
evidence: 'Compose-time suggestion is non-blocking, capped (3 to 5 results)'
'catch-up happens in the reader's process on next use, keyed by the tickets-branch HEAD SHA, with full rebuild on any mismatch'
'an LLM judge runs only on demand ... at most 2 LLM calls'
ABSENCE: no disposition word (retryable/transient vs fatal/permanent) is attached to the suggestion arm, the rebuild arm, or the judge arm
findings.finding: The plan gates in a failure path — compose-time suggestion is required to be 'non-blocking' and the reader does a 'full rebuild on any mismatch' / catch-up — but never states the failure-disposition contract: what the caller (rebar create / MCP / library) surfaces when the index is missing, catch-up/rebuild fails, embedding is unavailable, or the on-demand judge errors.
findings.location: Constraints ('Compose-time suggestion is non-blocking'; 'catch-up ... with full rebuild on any mismatch'); AC2; AC5
scenarios: Index rebuild fails mid-create — does create still succeed with an empty advisory field (degrade) or error?
The on-demand LLM judge hits a Bedrock 429 — is that surfaced as retryable (WAIT_AND_RETRY) or swallowed?
Embedding backend unreachable at compose time
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 'Failure-disposition contract' note to the ADR scope: suggestion failure degrades to an empty advisory field (non-fatal, create still succeeds); a tickets-branch SHA mismatch triggers a full rebuild (non-fatal, transparent); an LLM judge error preserves the underlying disposition (a retryable Bedrock 429 surfaces as retryable, never masked by the advisory path).

evidence: 2 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the minimum-title-length gate value (or a stated default) in AC2 and reference it from the constraint, so create-time surfacing's gating threshold is executable without clarification.
evidence: Constraint: 'Compose-time suggestion is non-blocking, capped (3 to 5 results), and gated on a minimum title length (Discourse, GitHub, Bugzilla).'
AC2 specifies the fields (id, alias, title, score), p95 and store size but is silent on a minimum-title-length gate or its value.
ABSENCE: no concrete character/token threshold is stated anywhere in the plan.
findings.finding: The constraints section mandates that compose-time suggestion is 'gated on a minimum title length', but AC2 (the create-time surfacing criterion) neither states the threshold value nor requires the create path to honor the gate, leaving the minimum length undefined for the executor.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, AC2 (rebar create returns top-5 similar tickets) vs Constraints ('gated on a minimum title length')
scenarios: Executor implements AC2 and must guess whether/what minimum title length gates the suggestion, or omits the gate entirely, violating the stated constraint.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to AC2 a concrete minimum, e.g. 'suggestions are suppressed for titles shorter than N characters', and assert it in the parity tests.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make candidate 3 (Titan embedding) entitlement a hard precondition for ADR finalization so the ADR cannot land selecting a non-vector architecture that contradicts the parent's operator framing.
evidence: Child: 'the Titan call is NOT entitled today... amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0 returns AccessDeniedException there... Candidate 3 is not [entitled].'

Child: 'The credentials-absent skip is widened to catch AccessDeniedException, recording candidate 3 unavailable with the error instead of aborting — and an unavailable candidate may not be selected by the ADR.'
Parent 'Operator framing (2026-09-06)': 'This is a vector search problem over summaries of large tickets. A lexical-only local index is insufficient and provably so against the historical corpus.'
Parent AC1 requires the ADR to record 'embedding model and store'; parent constraints require 'summarization and embedding run in a batch step'.
container pairing: parent + c670-c285-a0f9-4b40
findings.finding: Child c670 permits the vector candidate (candidate 3, Amazon Titan) to be recorded as 'unavailable' when the AWS entitlement is missing, and states 'an unavailable candidate may not be selected by the ADR' — which would force the ADR to name a lexical/digest architecture. This contradicts the parent's operator framing ('This is a vector search problem over summaries of large tickets. A lexical-only local index is insufficient and provably so') and leaves the deferred index child (parent AC2) with no chosen embedding model.
scenarios: The eval runs without Titan entitlement; candidate 3 is recorded unavailable; the ADR names a lexical/digest architecture to avoid an unselectable candidate.
Downstream 'Index and create-time surfacing' child inherits an ADR with no embedding model, contradicting the parent's required vector architecture and AC1's 'embedding model and store' field.
findings.suggested_fix: Require the Titan ARN be added to iam_s7.tf (or a developer identity with recorded entitlement) BEFORE the ADR is written, and state that the ADR may not be finalized while candidate 3 is 'unavailable', so the mandated vector architecture (and its embedding model, needed by the downstream index child) is always measured.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm parent AC2/AC3/AC4/AC5 are tracked as deferred children (created on ADR landing) and not treated as satisfied by the roster as it stands.
evidence: Parent 'Child decomposition': 'Index and create-time surfacing: delivers criteria 2, 3, 4.' and 'Plan-review overlap on demand: delivers criterion 5.' and 'Children after the first are created when the ADR lands.'
Complete sibling roster lists only c670-c285-a0f9-4b40; no child for criteria 2–5 is present.

Parent AC2 (top-5 across CLI/library/MCP, p95 500ms @10k), AC3 (no derived data on tickets branch), AC4 (findable by next create, no background process), AC5 (plan-review overlap, bounded judge) have no delivering sibling in the roster.
container pairing: parent + c670-c285-a0f9-4b40
findings.finding: Parent acceptance criteria AC2, AC3, AC4, and AC5 are not delivered by any sibling present in the roster; only child c670 (AC1) exists. The decomposition text states the remaining children are created after the ADR lands, so these four parent criteria are uncovered in the current roster.
findings.location: child c670-c285-a0f9-4b40 (roster coverage of parent AC2–AC5)
scenarios: A completion verifier run over the current roster would find parent AC2–AC5 with no delivering child.
If the epic were closed on the strength of the landed ADR, the create-time surfacing and plan-review surfaces (the actual user-facing capability) would never be built.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the two post-ADR children as explicit open items on the epic so the coverage gap for AC2–AC5 is visible until those children are created and their ACs parseable.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State in the ADR / implementation child whether the result cap, min-title-length gate, and judge budget are configurable (e.g. via rebar.toml) or deliberately fixed, with the rationale.
evidence: 'Compose-time suggestion is non-blocking, capped (3 to 5 results), and gated on a minimum title length'
'an LLM judge runs only on demand over at most 10 lexical-or-vector candidates'
'a bounded judge budget (at most 10 candidates, at most 2 LLM calls)'
findings.finding: The thresholds introduced as design constraints — result cap (3 to 5), minimum title length gate, judge budget (at most 10 candidates / at most 2 LLM calls) — are stated as fixed values but the plan does not say whether they are configurable or hardcoded.
findings.location: Constraints every design must satisfy; AC2; AC5
scenarios: Operator wants to tune result cap or min-title-length per store without a code change

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Require the ADR (AC1) to record the embedding provider's auth/HTTPS/egress precondition -- whether the chosen embedding model reuses the existing Anthropic/Bedrock credential seam or introduces a new provider, auth scope, and egress path -- as part of justifying the 'embedding model and store' choice.
evidence: AC1 lists deliverables as 'summarization method, embedding model and store, index location and freshness key, catch-up strategy' but names no auth/transport precondition for the embedding provider
Constraint 'Model calls are bounded and off the write path: summarization and embedding run in a batch step' asserts embedding calls will happen but states no provider/auth/HTTPS precondition

Codebase has no embedding provider seam: src/rebar/llm/providers.py builds text-completion providers only; ADR 0086 states the v1 design stayed 'Anthropic-only, no-heavy-ML grain (no vector DB, no new dependency)'
resolve_symbol: 'voyageai' and 'anthropic.embeddings' both UNRESOLVED in the installed environment (not proof of absence, but confirms no embedding client is wired today)

Evidence class: Partially-verified -- embedding/vector-search as a capability is real and the gap is correctly routed to the research child, but the concrete provider surface and its auth/egress are (by design) unconfirmed
findings.finding: The plan introduces a new embedding-model + vector-store capability the repo has never used (existing LLM infra is text-completion only via pydantic-ai; ADR 0086 explicitly chose no embeddings/no vector DB/no new dependency), but neither the OSS-survey constraints nor AC1 require the ADR to state the embedding provider's auth / HTTPS / egress precondition -- i.e. whether the chosen embedding model reuses the existing Anthropic/Bedrock credential path or introduces a new provider, new auth scope, and new egress.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria (AC1) / Constraints every design must satisfy
scenarios: The ADR lands choosing an embedding model reachable only via a new provider/credential that the current Anthropic/Bedrock-only auth seam does not cover, discovered only at implementation child time
The chosen embedding model requires network egress/HTTPS to a vendor not previously contacted, surfacing a new secret/egress precondition after the architecture is committed
findings.suggested_fix: Add to AC1's parenthetical deliverable list (or the Constraints block) that the ADR must state the embedding provider, its auth mechanism and transport (HTTPS/egress), and whether it reuses the existing provider seam in src/rebar/llm/providers.py or requires a new one; the research child should verify reachability under the chosen credential path before the implementation children are created.
